title: Internal-Hom cancellation by an invertible tensor factor
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a monoidal category [def-sfb-monoidal-category] with a symmetric braiding $\sigma_{U,V}:U\otimes V\xrightarrow{\sim}V\otimes U$, natural in both variables and satisfying the hexagon and symmetry identities. Suppose it is closed: for every $X$ there is a functor $[X,-]$ and adjunction bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(Z\otimes X,Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Z,[X,Y])$, natural in $X,Y,Z$. Write $e_{X,Y}:[X,Y]\otimes X\to Y$ for evaluation. Let $J,I\in\mathcal C$ have specified isomorphisms $J\otimes I\cong\mathbf1$ and $I\otimes J\cong\mathbf1$; this is the meaning of an invertible tensor factor here. For all $X,Y$ define two morphisms by transposition:
$$t_{X,Y,J}:[X,Y]\otimes J\longrightarrow[X,Y\otimes J],\qquad s_{X,Y,J}:[X,Y]\longrightarrow[X\otimes J,Y\otimes J],$$
where their uncurrying equations, with associators suppressed, are
$$e_{X,Y\otimes J}\circ(t_{X,Y,J}\otimes1_X)=(e_{X,Y}\otimes1_J)\circ(1_{[X,Y]}\otimes\sigma_{J,X}),$$
$$e_{X\otimes J,Y\otimes J}\circ(s_{X,Y,J}\otimes1_{X\otimes J})=e_{X,Y}\otimes1_J.$$
Both $t_{X,Y,J}$ and $s_{X,Y,J}$ are isomorphisms, natural contravariantly in $X$ and covariantly in $Y$. They are also compatible with isomorphisms of the invertible factor $J$. In particular $c_{X,Y,J}=s_{X,Y,J}^{-1}$ is the canonical cancellation isomorphism $[X\otimes J,Y\otimes J]\xrightarrow{\sim}[X,Y]$, and the displayed equations specify the evaluation normalization of these isomorphisms and their inverses.
